title: stop() aborts the long poll instead of waiting out the server's deadline
why: A long poll can hold the connection for the full timeout — up to 30 seconds by contract. An SDK that only sets a flag and waits for the request to come back makes every shutdown take that long: a deploy hangs, a Ctrl-C feels broken, and a supervisor that kills after 10s leaves the process no chance to stop cleanly. The server here holds the response for five seconds and stop() is called after two hundred milliseconds; returning promptly is the whole guarantee.
